events.title: U.S. conducts new strikes after alleged Iranian violations
events.summary: U.S. forces conduct new strikes after renewed accusations of Iranian violations, demonstrating that the MoU has already begun to fray operationally.
events.context: The memorandum's maritime ambiguity quickly became an operational dispute. Iran claimed authority to regulate transit, whereas Washington and Gulf partners insisted that reopening had to mean unrestricted commercial passage.
details: CENTCOM said renewed strikes targeted missile and drone stores and coastal radar after the previous day's attack on a commercial ship. Iranian accounts reported an incident at Sirik and retaliatory action against U.S. bases; reporting about damage at the port itself was inconsistent.

The two governments were reading the June agreement differently. Iran's insistence on its transit procedures could coexist, in its account, with reopening Hormuz; the American interpretation rejected restrictions and tolls. This disagreement helps explain why a signed framework failed to prevent another round of strikes, without establishing which side's account of each attack was correct.

events.title: CENTCOM begins new large-scale strike wave after tanker incidents
events.summary: After three commercial vessels or tankers are struck by projectiles around Hormuz, CENTCOM begins a new large-scale strike wave against Iran.
events.context: The July escalation combined renewed bombing with the withdrawal of economic relief. Attacks on commercial vessels became the immediate setting for abandoning practical concessions made under the June framework.
details: Reuters reported that three tankers had been hit by projectiles around Hormuz before the United States launched another substantial wave of strikes. The maritime incidents were reported through security and official channels; they do not independently establish every detail of the American attribution.

Washington also revoked the licence that had allowed Iranian oil sales under the interim agreement. That economic reversal made the episode more than a brief exchange of fire: the incentives intended to sustain the negotiating period were being dismantled alongside the military escalation. Iran continued to insist that Washington had violated the memorandum.
events.research_note: Reuters reports checked. The renewed strike wave is corroborated, but the identity of each attacker and the justification for every target were not independently verified. Oil-licence revocation is treated separately from the later presidential declaration that the MoU was over.

events.title: CENTCOM says it hits more than 80 targets
events.summary: CENTCOM says it hits more than 80 targets, including Iranian air defences, command-and-control facilities, coastal radar, anti-ship missile infrastructure and more than 60 IRGC small boats.
events.context: CENTCOM's target count described the scale it claimed for the operation, not an independently audited tally of destroyed assets. The emphasis on boats and coastal systems reflected Washington's stated effort to reduce threats to shipping.
details: The U.S. military reported striking more than 80 targets, including air defences, command facilities, radar and anti-ship infrastructure. Its account also listed more than 60 Revolutionary Guard small boats. These figures are a military operational announcement and should not be added together as though they necessarily represented separate, non-overlapping categories.

The claimed mix of targets connects the bombing campaign to the fight over maritime access. It does not demonstrate that Iran had lost the ability to threaten navigation or that every vessel struck was preparing an imminent attack. Reporting the announcement as such preserves the distinction between operation size, damage assessment and strategic effect.

events.title: U.S. withdraws the Iranian oil-sales waiver granted under the June framework
events.summary: OFAC revokes General License X and replaces it with a narrow wind-down authorization. The new license permits specified closing transactions only until 12:01 a.m. U.S. Eastern time on 17 July, rather than continuing the June waiver to August.
events.intro: The removal of this economic concession preceded Trump’s 8 July statement that the memorandum was over.
events.context: The framework unravelled through concrete policy reversals as well as public rhetoric. The dated Treasury documents let the withdrawal of oil-sales permission be distinguished from the following day’s presidential declaration.
details: OFAC’s 7 July bulletin revoked the authorization issued in June and published General License X-1 in its place. The replacement did not preserve a general right to initiate new purchases or loadings: it covered transactions necessary to wind down activity previously permitted, subject to its stated exceptions and conditions.

The wind-down deadline was 12:01 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time on 17 July, equivalent to 04:01 UTC. Reuters’ subsequent account of Trump’s 8 July remarks placed the waiver withdrawal within the breakdown of the interim accord. This record establishes the dated change in U.S. sanctions policy; it does not assume that one government’s declaration settled every legal question about the memorandum.

Regional retaliation also widened as the June framework unravelled. events.summary: U.S. strikes continue. Washington reimposes a naval blockade effective that evening.
events.context: Washington restored a restriction directed at Iranian ports while still advocating passage for other commercial shipping. That distinction separated the U.S. blockade from Iran's competing restrictions on Hormuz transit.
details: A U.S. maritime advisory announced enforcement from 20:00 GMT on 14 July, equivalent to 21:00 in London. It applied to vessels entering or leaving Iranian ports and oil terminals regardless of flag, rather than announcing a ban on every ship moving through the strait.

The renewed blockade accompanied further strikes and threats against Iranian infrastructure. Its practical purpose was coercive economic pressure, but it also complicated the maritime provisions of the June framework. Describing both sides simply as 'closing Hormuz' would conceal their different announced targets and the exposure of neutral shipping to overlapping enforcement systems.
events.research_note: Contemporary Reuters report of the maritime advisory checked. Effective time and scope are distinguished from a claim that enforcement was complete everywhere. The event date remains 14 July.

events.title: U.S. strikes Greater Tunb and southern Iranian coastal sites
events.summary: U.S. attacks include Greater Tunb and southern Iranian coastal sites. Iran reports fatalities at Bampour. A reported strike on a wheat silo becomes disputed, with Washington denying responsibility.
events.context: The day's reporting combined a U.S.-announced strike on island defences with Iranian reports of military deaths inland and a separate dispute over civilian infrastructure. These components have different sources and should not be presented as one independently verified target list.
details: CENTCOM said it conducted a 90-minute operation against coastal defences and cruise-missile sites on Greater Tunb, followed by another wave against military capabilities including facilities at Bandar Abbas. Iran's state broadcaster reported that an overnight strike on Bampour barracks killed at least seven members of the 388th Mechanized Infantry Brigade.

Separately, Iranian media alleged that a civilian wheat-storage facility at Hoveyzeh had been struck on 14 July. CENTCOM denied that allegation on 15 July and listed military targets it said had been attacked. The denial does not settle the underlying dispute, just as the Iranian allegation does not independently identify who caused the reported damage.
events.research_note: All three components have event-specific reporting. Target descriptions are U.S. claims, Bampour casualties an Iranian military/state-media report, and Hoveyzeh attribution disputed. The alleged silo incident dates to 14 July; the U.S. denial dates to 15 July.

events.title: Iran reports inland explosions and Tehran air-defence activity amid U.S. strikes
events.summary: Reuters relays Iranian reports of explosions at Khondab and air-defence activity in Tehran while U.S. strikes continue. CENTCOM separately says it disabled an unladen tanker heading toward Kharg; a strike on Tehran itself is not independently confirmed.
events.context: The source record supports a widening field of reported explosions and Iranian air-defence activity, but not a confirmed strike on Tehran itself. A tanker disabled by U.S. forces was a separate maritime enforcement action.
details: Reuters reported Iranian-media accounts of explosions at Khondab, southwest of Tehran, and the activation of air defences in the capital against perceived threats. Most detailed strike reporting still concerned southern and coastal locations. Air-defence activation is not proof that a bomb hit a particular site in Tehran.

CENTCOM separately said an unladen tanker heading toward Kharg ignored warnings and was disabled by missiles fired into its smokestack. That action was reported late on 15 July and in 16 July coverage. It illustrates escalation of blockade enforcement but should not be used as evidence for an independently confirmed northward air campaign.

events.title: Daily U.S. strikes continue as Iran retaliates and tanker accounts conflict
events.summary: U.S. strikes and Iranian regional retaliation continue. U.S. Marines board a tanker, while Iran reports explosions involving two tankers and the U.S. military rejects that account.
events.context: The daily campaign was becoming an infrastructure and maritime confrontation, not simply a repetition of the initial coastal raids. Both sides were also issuing incompatible accounts of events involving tankers.
details: Reuters described the United States beginning a seventh consecutive night on 17 July after completion of the sixth overnight sequence. The difference explains why contemporary headlines used both counts; a date-based record is clearer than treating them as competing totals for the same completed operation.

U.S. Marines boarded a tanker near Hormuz while Iranian media claimed that two oil tankers had exploded after entering a mined route. The U.S. military rejected that tanker report. Regional attack claims likewise require attribution: a list of countries mentioned in military statements is not, by itself, an independently confirmed list of bases damaged.

events.title: Iranian attack in Jordan kills two U.S. military personnel

events.context: The two American deaths were announced on 18 July but occurred during the attack on Friday, 17 July. The initial missing-person report should be retained as a time-specific status, not assumed to be the final outcome.
details: CENTCOM said two service members died while defending against Iranian missiles and drones in Jordan. Initial reporting also listed another service member as missing. That announcement changed the human stakes of a campaign that Washington had repeatedly described in terms of limited operations and protection of shipping.

Later Pentagon notices identified the Jordan casualties and subsequently confirmed an additional death from that attack. The separate ordnance-disposal death in Iraq did not account for the initially missing person in Jordan. Keeping these incidents apart prevents the running casualty chronology from implying that three people died in one location or operation.

events.title: U.S. service member dies during drone-ordnance disposal in northern Iraq
events.summary: A U.S. service member dies on 18 July during a controlled detonation of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian drone in northern Iraq. CENTCOM announces the death on 19 July; it is separate from the Jordan attack.
events.context: This death arose during disposal of unexploded ordnance in northern Iraq, not from the Iranian attack in Jordan. It illustrates a distinct operational hazard continuing after a drone has been brought down.
details: CENTCOM said a U.S. service member died on Saturday, 18 July, during a controlled detonation of unexploded material from a downed Iranian drone. The statement was reported on Sunday, 19 July. The base entry therefore uses the disclosure date rather than the death date.

Subsequent military reporting named the soldier as Sergeant Michael Emmanuel Swinton and said the death was under investigation. The word 'third' reflects the order of early public announcements, not the eventual combined death toll: another Jordan casualty was subsequently confirmed. The Iraq and Jordan incidents should remain separate in both geography and causation.

events.title: Trump vows retaliation; Houthis announce Saudi naval-blockade campaign
events.summary: Trump says Iran will pay many times over for U.S. deaths. The Houthis separately announce a naval-blockade campaign against Saudi Arabia following attacks on Yemen.
events.context: The announcement brought the Red Sea and Saudi shipping more directly into the escalation. Houthi threats threatened a second maritime route at the same time that Hormuz remained contested.
details: The Houthis declared a naval-blockade campaign against Saudi Arabia after attacks on Yemen, prompting a warning of a firm response from the Saudi-led coalition. Their declaration was a threat and an announced policy, not evidence that all access to Saudi ports had actually ceased.

Trump separately promised retaliation for American service-member deaths while U.S. strikes continued. The two announcements should be read as parallel escalatory developments, not proof that the Houthis acted under a newly issued Iranian order. The danger was a widening regional confrontation in which alternatives to Hormuz could themselves become unsafe.
events.research_note: Contemporary Reuters reports checked. The Houthi campaign is verified as an announcement, not as an effective comprehensive blockade. No direct command relationship for this particular action was independently established.

events.title: U.S. strikes around Bushehr, Ahvaz and Jask
events.summary: CENTCOM reports another round of strikes on military capabilities, while Iranian media report attacks in southern Iran. Trump also threatens future strikes on bridges and power plants.
events.context: American operations were being sustained as a daily campaign, with maritime protection increasingly paired with threats against civilian-use infrastructure. The announced targets and the locations of reported explosions came from different sources.
details: CENTCOM said the 12th consecutive round targeted maritime capabilities, drone and missile storage, coastal surveillance and air defences. Its previous night's official release likewise described attacks on operational centres and military logistics. These statements explain the military's announced mission but do not independently demonstrate destruction of every target.

Iranian-media reports named Bushehr, Ahvaz and Jask among locations attacked. Separately, Trump threatened to respond to future attacks on ships by destroying a bridge or power plant. That threatened expansion is analytically distinct from the targets CENTCOM said had already been hit, and should not be presented as an accomplished infrastructure campaign.

events.title: Fighting continues across Iran, Gulf and Red Sea theatres
events.summary: U.S. strikes continue; Iranian attacks affect Kuwait and Jordan; a tanker catches fire around Hormuz. Houthis separately claim attacks on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea.
events.context: The Red Sea incidents threatened Saudi export routes that could otherwise reduce reliance on Hormuz. This made the Houthi claims strategically significant even where details of individual attacks were unconfirmed.
details: The Houthis said they attacked two Saudi tankers. Saudi reporting confirmed a fire involving Encelia, while Reuters could not independently confirm the reported second tanker, Layla. The asymmetry in confirmation is important: two claims did not automatically amount to two independently verified strikes.

At Hormuz, Iranian reporting also described a tanker fire associated with a purportedly mined route. These claims accompanied continuing U.S. operations and regional retaliation, but they were separate incidents with different evidence. Combining them into a single confirmed regional damage tally would erase the uncertainty surrounding vessel identities, weapons and reported outcomes.

events.title: U.S. pauses strikes and Iran reciprocally halts major retaliation
events.summary: After a 24 July U.S. security meeting, no further bombing round follows overnight after 13 consecutive nights. A mediator describes reduced Iranian counterstrikes; the U.S. maritime blockade continues.
events.context: The pause was a temporary reduction in bombing, not a new comprehensive ceasefire. Maritime enforcement and other regional hostilities continued, leaving diplomacy room to operate without ending coercion.
details: AP reported that Trump met senior national-security aides on Friday, 24 July, and no new U.S. bombing round followed overnight after 13 consecutive nights. A regional mediator described pauses in American strikes and Iranian counterstrikes as a positive signal, while warning that the diplomatic position was still unsettled.

The U.S. blockade continued; the military said it disabled a ship attempting to breach it on Friday. Houthi activity also continued in the Red Sea theatre. Those developments show why this event should be bounded as a late-July operational lull, not treated as an uninterrupted peace extending to the end of August.

relationships.label: Renewed strike after an interrupted pause
relationships.summary: The late-July pause was interrupted by confirmed U.S. strikes on 29 July and a further suspension announced on 1 August. The 30 August Larak strike followed that later lull, not an uninterrupted ceasefire beginning on 24 July.

events.research_note: AP syndicated article opened and read. The decision/no-strike sequence spans 24–25 July, so an overnight range is more defensible than an exact unqualified start time. Later reporting identifies additional late-July strikes and a separate 1 August pause; the lulls must not be merged.

revisions.reason: AP places the decision and first no-strike interval across the Friday–Saturday boundary. The pause was not an end to all regional hostilities.

previous.summary: After nearly two weeks of renewed fighting, the United States pauses strikes and Iran reciprocally halts major retaliatory operations.

events.title: Military pause holds amid conflicting claims about talks
events.summary: The pause broadly holds. Trump says good talks are under way; Iranian officials publicly deny seeking direct negotiations and insist that Tehran still controls Hormuz.
events.context: The lull allowed intermediaries to explore maritime arrangements, but Washington and Tehran described the diplomatic channel differently. A claim that contacts were productive did not establish that direct U.S.–Iran negotiations had resumed.
details: During the 25–27 July interval, Iran maintained that it controlled Hormuz and publicly denied seeking talks. Trump said discussions were going well. Reuters reported these incompatible public accounts as the bombing pause extended through the weekend.

Iran–Oman technical contacts and broader mediation could proceed even while Tehran denied direct talks with Washington. This distinction helps reconcile apparently contradictory headlines without deciding that either side had conceded its central position. Reports of other regional incidents also mean that a pause in the main air campaign should not be equated with complete silence across every theatre.
events.research_note: Reuters reporting checked. Retains the 25–27 July interval and locates the explicit conflicting statements on 27 July. These sources establish a temporary pause, not continuous cessation through 30 August or a completed negotiating agreement.

events.title: Mediation efforts resume after military pause
events.summary: Mediation efforts resume through intermediaries following the military pause.
events.context: Mediation focused increasingly on whether a practical shipping arrangement could be reached without settling every aspect of the war. Proposals about transit fees revealed the distance between restoring movement and agreeing who controlled the strait.
details: Reuters reported Gulf support for an Omani proposal involving voluntary fees for passage. That was a negotiating idea, not a publicly implemented toll system or Iranian acceptance of unrestricted navigation. The distinction matters because both governments could claim to favour reopening while attaching incompatible conditions.

Trump again described contacts as positive while repeating threats against Iranian infrastructure. Iranian denials of seeking direct talks did not rule out messages through regional intermediaries. The available evidence supports active mediation and competing proposals, but not a concluded agreement or a precisely documented new formal negotiating round on this date.
events.research_note: Contemporaneous Reuters reports checked. Proposed fees and diplomatic progress remain reported proposals and assessments. No new signed arrangement or independently documented direct U.S.–Iran meeting is asserted.

events.title: Trump says parties have reached the perimeters of a deal
events.summary: In a post made late on 1 August U.S. Eastern time—early 2 August in London—Trump says an outline of a deal has been reached and cancels planned strikes while keeping forces ready.
events.context: This statement belongs to a separate early-August suspension of planned attacks. Its late-July placement confuses two pauses and makes the subsequent escalation chronology misleading.
details: The archived Truth Social post containing the distinctive 'perimeters of a deal' wording is timestamped 1 August at 10:05 p.m. U.S. Eastern time. That is 2 August at 03:05 in London. Trump said he was cancelling planned strikes after requests from Gulf leaders while keeping forces ready to attack.

Euronews and CBS reported the announcement that weekend. The language described an outline and an expectation of agreement, not signed final terms. Because late-July fighting had not ended in one continuous pause, correcting this date also prevents the Larak strike from being measured against the wrong cessation point.

sources.publisher: Trump's Truth archive of presidential post

events.research_note: Exact archived post timestamp and independent weekend reporting checked. Proposes 2 August for a Europe/London calendar, preserving the U.S.-local 1 August date in prose. The 27 July date is not supported for this wording; mutable live-blog publication metadata should not override the post timestamp.

revisions.reason: The archived post is timestamped 1 August 22:05 EDT, or 2 August 03:05 BST. The proposed date follows the dataset's Europe/London timezone; the existing 27 July placement is contradicted.

events.title: Trump gives Iran one last chance before decapitation
events.summary: Trump tells Iran it has one last chance before decapitation to make an agreement. Unlike March and April, he provides no specific number of hours or days. Tehran says no direct talks are under way while Trump says discussions are occurring.
events.context: The threat followed another announced pause and again left the deadline undefined. Trump described talks as active while Iran denied that direct negotiations were taking place.
details: In Oval Office remarks, Trump warned of a severe attack if Iran failed to make an agreement and called the opportunity a final chance. Reuters recorded him describing discussions as ongoing, including contacts involving regional states.

The statement supplied no number of hours or days and no published set of terms whose acceptance would settle the issue. Its function was coercive signalling rather than a verifiable countdown. Public disagreement about whether talks existed also requires attention to the channel: exchanges through mediators are not necessarily the direct negotiations Tehran was denying.
events.research_note: Reuters report and indexed pool-video transcript checked. The threat is an official statement, not confirmation of an approved strike or fixed deadline. No precise countdown should be generated from this language.

events.title: Iran disputes relevance of the memorandum's reported 60-day deadline
events.summary: Iran says the June memorandum's reported negotiating deadline has lost relevance because of U.S. violations and the failure to hold the envisaged talks. Contemporaneous reporting did not establish an unambiguous start for the 60-day clock.
events.context: By mid-August, the dispute concerned whether the June framework still had practical relevance, not simply whether a clearly agreed clock had run out. Fighting and incompatible interpretations had already undermined its negotiating process.
details: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said the reported 60-day period had lost its relevance because Washington had violated the memorandum and the envisaged talks had not proceeded. His position was an Iranian argument about the agreement's operation, not proof that the draft had never contained a negotiating period.

Reuters's June draft explicitly envisaged up to 60 days, extendable by agreement, while contemporary signature reporting left the precise start uncertain. A report describing 17 August as the expiry date therefore cannot justify an exact universal countdown. The secure event on this date is Iran's public rejection of the deadline's relevance.

events.research_note: Contemporary 17 August statement reports and the earlier Reuters draft checked. Proposes reframing the primary title as a dispute over the reported deadline, not a mathematically certain expiry. An agreed clock-start instrument or mutually confirmed extension was not located.

revisions.reason: The verified dated event is Baghaei's statement. An exact contractual expiry on 17 August is not established by the available signature and draft evidence.

events.title: Washington intensifies secondary-sanctions campaign
events.summary: Washington intensifies its secondary-sanctions campaign, targeting banks and entities accused of enabling Iranian trade and sanction evasion.
events.context: Washington shifted pressure toward foreign financial institutions and trade intermediaries whose access to the American system could be threatened. The policy sought to isolate Iranian commerce without assuming that bombing alone would produce a settlement.
details: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced an expanded economic campaign and warned foreign institutions against enabling Iranian activity. Reuters reported that the administration was stopping short, at that point, of its most sweeping possible measures against major Chinese banks despite China's role as an important buyer of Iranian oil.

The announcement combined new pressure with warnings about future enforcement. It should not be described as an immediate blanket sanction on every country trading with Iran. The historical change was the increased emphasis on third-country exposure and financial access while the military and diplomatic confrontation remained unresolved.
events.research_note: Reuters article and indexed briefing account checked. The dossier distinguishes a campaign announcement and prospective threats from completed designation of every institution mentioned. It is a historical account, not guidance on any person's sanctions obligations.

events.title: Trump says international waters in Hormuz have been demined
events.summary: Trump says international waters in Hormuz have been demined, warning of zero tolerance for new Iranian mines.
events.context: Trump's declaration of cleared international waters was intended to reassure shipping while warning Iran against renewed mine-laying. It did not establish that the strait had returned to normal commercial use.
details: The president said mines in international waters had been removed or detonated and threatened vessels attempting to lay new ones. This was a U.S. official assessment of a maritime-clearance effort, not an independently certified guarantee that every route was safe.

Reuters cited Vortexa estimates of about five million barrels a day moving through the strait, compared with roughly twenty million before the war. Continued low traffic reflected the difference between a claim about mines and the wider risks created by threats, competing transit rules and renewed hostilities. The claim should therefore remain attributed rather than be displayed as confirmed complete demining.
events.research_note: Reuters report checked. Proposes 'official_claim' for the mine-clearance assessment. No independent comprehensive mine survey or safety certification was examined; traffic estimates are not a direct measurement of mines remaining.

revisions.reason: Complete mine clearance is the president's assessment; no independent comprehensive clearance certification was examined.

events.title: Pakistan reports significant progress during Munir's Tehran visit
events.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi reports significant progress during Asim Munir's meetings with Iranian leaders, including discussions of Hormuz. The U.S. does not immediately confirm a breakthrough.
events.context: Pakistan's renewed diplomatic effort centred on Asim Munir's access to Iranian leaders and discussion of Hormuz. The reported progress was Islamabad's assessment, not a jointly published U.S.–Iran agreement.
details: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi described significant progress while accompanying Munir in Tehran. Pakistani military reporting described meetings with Iranian leaders about de-escalation, maritime access and ending the conflict, following a call between Munir and Trump before the visit.

The U.S. government did not immediately confirm a breakthrough in the Reuters account. This limits the conclusion that can be drawn: the visit demonstrates an active intermediary channel and Pakistani optimism, but not acceptance by Washington of specific Iranian conditions or a completed settlement ready for implementation.

events.title: U.S. begins returning diplomatic personnel to regional posts
events.summary: The United States begins returning some diplomatic personnel to Middle Eastern posts evacuated or reduced during the conflict.
events.context: The staffing decision suggested a partial normalisation of diplomatic operations without proving the military crisis had ended. Returning personnel and planned staffing levels were different stages of the process.
details: Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter, reported that the United States had begun returning personnel to posts including Lebanon, Israel, Saudi Arabia and Baghdad. The account also described differentiated future staffing plans across the region rather than a simultaneous return of every evacuated mission to full capacity.

The State Department's public response referred to continuing review of security conditions instead of confirming every operational detail. The episode is therefore best read as a reported, selective reversal of evacuations. It does not establish that all dependants had returned, that every embassy was fully staffed or that Washington considered further conflict impossible.

events.title: Qatar's prime minister travels to Tehran for mediation

events.context: Qatar's visit sought an interim maritime mechanism while the wider settlement remained stalled. Its proposals linked navigation and mine clearance rather than treating reopening as a purely rhetorical declaration.
details: Qatar announced the visit on 26 August, but its official Foreign Ministry records date the Tehran meetings to 27 August. Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

Qatar's readout described efforts involving a temporary joint shipping corridor and mine clearance, alongside de-escalation and respect for freedom of navigation. The proposals were not an agreement already in force. They also show why regional mediation could continue while Washington publicly said it was not currently negotiating with Iran.

events.summary: Iran says it is preparing conditions for restoring normal Hormuz traffic after mediation. Previous demands included ending the U.S. blockade, compensation and sanctions relief; Iran–Oman arrangements remain under discussion.
events.context: Iran was preparing a list of conditions after renewed mediation, not necessarily unveiling a completed new package. Existing demands about the blockade, sanctions and compensation remained the background to that exercise.
details: Following Qatar's Tehran visit, Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei said Iran would set out conditions for restoring normal transit. Reuters distinguished this prospective list from earlier Iranian demands, and reported uncertainty over whether Tehran would change its position enough to make an agreement possible.

Iranian officials also described progress with Oman on a corridor using both countries' waters. These discussions did not resolve the disagreement between U.S. assertions that international lanes were open and Iranian insistence that vessels required permission.

Trump also publicly said he was not currently talking to Iran. That statement can be established independently of the reported message about the memorandum, but neither establishes that regional mediation had stopped. events.title: IRGC Navy says Iran retains full control of Hormuz
events.summary: The IRGC Navy says Iran retains full control of the Strait and will maintain restrictions until the United States ends military action and fulfils previous commitments.
events.context: The IRGC's control claim directly challenged American assertions that shipping lanes were open. Traffic observations showed continued use of the strait, but at a level consistent with severe restrictions rather than normality.
details: The IRGC Navy said vessels still required Iranian permission and that restrictions would continue until Washington ended military action and honoured earlier commitments. This was a statement of intended authority over passage, not independent proof that Iran controlled every movement through the waterway.

Reuters contrasted the statement with shipping data showing only seven visible commodity-vessel transits on 27 August, compared with seventeen the preceding day. Such counts help test sweeping reopening claims but cannot reveal every vessel, especially when position transmitters are switched off. Neither side's political slogan adequately described that uneven, risky traffic.

'Full control' remains explicitly an IRGC claim; observed traffic does not independently settle sovereignty or enforcement.

events.title: U.S. forces strike two Iranian launchers on Larak Island
events.summary: U.S. forces strike two launchers on Larak Island. CENTCOM says IRGC personnel were preparing rockets carrying sea mines; Iranian reporting describes a drone attack. AP identifies 29 July as the previous confirmed U.S. strike date and a further suspension announced on 1 August.
events.intro: The U.S. targeted two launchers it said were preparing rockets carrying sea mines; Iran reported casualties and answered with regional attacks.
events.context: Larak returned the confrontation to the immediate approaches to Hormuz just days after Washington claimed shipping lanes had been cleared of mines. The strike's occurrence is corroborated, but the alleged imminent threat remains the U.S. military's account of why it acted.
details: U.S. forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island on 30 August. CENTCOM spokesperson Tim Hawkins said Revolutionary Guard forces had been preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the strait. That wording is more specific than separate preparations of rockets and mines, and it should remain attributed rather than be presented as an independently observed payload.

Iranian outlets reported explosions, and the IRGC said fighters and civilians were killed or injured. Tasnim described a drone attack; the publicly reported U.S. confirmation did not independently settle the aircraft type. RFE/RL also obtained U.S. official confirmation of the launcher strike, strengthening occurrence verification without independently proving every targeting claim.

AP placed the previous confirmed U.S. strikes on 29 July and the later announced suspension on 1 August. Those dates distinguish this month-long lull from the earlier 24–27 July pause. Iran's subsequent attacks toward bases in Jordan extended into 31 August regional time, so the strike and retaliation should not be forced into a single local calendar day.

previous.summary: U.S. drones strike two Iranian rocket-launch positions on Larak Island. Washington says IRGC personnel were preparing rockets and naval mines. It is the first acknowledged U.S. strike on Iran since the late-July pause.

events.title: Iran reports casualties from Larak strike
events.summary: Iran says the Larak attack killed or injured fighters and civilians.
events.context: Iran's initial casualty statement established that Tehran acknowledged human losses while leaving their scale and composition unclear. It did not provide a count that could be safely entered into a cumulative death toll.
details: The Revolutionary Guards said the U.S. attack caused deaths and injuries among fighters and compatriots, wording Reuters rendered as involving fighters and civilians. The initial statement did not distinguish the number killed from the number wounded or provide a verified civilian–military breakdown.

Washington's explanation focused on an alleged mine-laying threat, whereas Iran emphasised casualties and promised punishment. These accounts address different issues: a claimed military target does not disprove civilian harm, and an unspecified casualty statement does not independently identify victims or establish the full circumstances of the strike.
events.research_note: Reuters account of the initial Iranian statement checked. No numerical casualty total is inferred from 'several', and killed/wounded categories are not merged. Independent victim identification and the initial civilian/combatant split remain unverified.

events.title: Iran claims strikes toward Jordan bases; Jordan reports eight interceptions
events.summary: Iran says it launches ballistic missiles toward the King Hussein and Al-Azraq bases in response to Larak. Jordan reports intercepting eight missiles at dawn on 31 August, with no civilian or property harm in its initial account.
events.context: Iran linked the missile launches to the Larak strike, extending the response to U.S. forces hosted by Jordan. Jordan's interception report corroborated incoming missiles but did not validate every Iranian claim about targets or effect.
details: The IRGC said it had fired ballistic missiles toward the King Hussein and Al-Azraq bases in response to the American attack. Jordan's military said it intercepted eight missiles at dawn on Monday, 31 August, before they harmed civilians or property.

Those accounts are stronger evidence for a cross-border missile incident than for successful strikes on either base. Initial reporting described no major damage; this is not the same as an exhaustive independent base assessment. The date also crosses the U.S.–Middle East news boundary: coverage began on 30 August, but Jordan's reported interceptions occurred the following morning.
search_aliases: Iran launches ballistic missiles toward two U.S. bases in Jordan
events.research_note: Reuters statement report and The National article opened/checked. Proposes an overnight 30–31 August range or a clearly labelled 31 August interception event. Targets are Iran's claim; eight interceptions are Jordan's account; successful base hits were not independently confirmed.

revisions.reason: The Iranian claim and Jordanian interception announcement span the overnight boundary. Successful hits on both bases were not independently established.

previous.title: Iran launches ballistic missiles toward two U.S. bases in Jordan
previous.summary: Iran retaliates by launching ballistic missiles toward two U.S. bases in Jordan. Most are intercepted and no major damage is reported.

events.title: Iran claims attack on UAE's Al Minhad Air Base
events.summary: Iran's army claims a drone attack on Al Minhad Air Base on 31 August. The UAE reports dealing with an Iranian drone over its waters and denies reports of a missile attack on the base; a successful base strike is not independently confirmed.
events.context: The Iranian claim and the UAE denial referred to different weapon descriptions, a distinction lost in simplified retellings. A reported intercepted drone does not establish that Al Minhad Air Base was hit.
details: On 31 August, Iran's army said it used drones against U.S. personnel and helicopters at Al Minhad, describing the action as retaliation for Larak. Reuters reported the claim through Iranian state television without independent confirmation of a successful strike.

The UAE said it had dealt with a drone coming from Iran over territorial waters and denied media reports of a missile attack on the base. That denial should not be silently rewritten as a detailed rebuttal of every element of the Iranian drone claim. The most defensible record is an unverified base-attack claim alongside the UAE's separately worded interception and denial statements.
events.research_note: Event-specific Reuters and UAE-response reporting checked. Proposes 31 August and wording distinguishing drones from the denied missile reports. The base-hit claim remains unverified/contradicted; no independent damage evidence was located.

revisions.reason: The dated Iranian statement is Monday, 31 August. Drone claims and the specifically worded missile denial must not be conflated.

previous.summary: Iran claims an attack on the UAE's Al Minhad Air Base. The UAE denies that the claimed strike succeeded.

events.title: Trump posts AI-generated video appearing to show Kharg Island destroyed
events.summary: Trump posts an AI-generated video appearing to show Iran's Kharg Island being destroyed and writes that the island is being blown to smithereens. The Pentagon and White House do not substantiate a new attack and Iranian and NIOC officials say Kharg remains operational.
events.context: The video was a genuine presidential social-media post but not evidence of a real attack on Kharg. It appeared alongside actual fighting at Larak, a different island hundreds of kilometres away.
details: Reuters reported that the clip was most likely synthetically generated, based on software analysis, and found no evidence of a new Kharg attack in the hours after the post. The White House and Pentagon did not immediately substantiate the apparent destruction. The posting was described as Sunday in the U.S., with reactions reported on Monday.

National Iranian Oil Company chief Hamid Bovard said operations at Kharg continued while earlier damage was repaired. That was an Iranian official account, not an independent site inspection, but it contradicted the impression conveyed by the video. Keeping synthetic imagery separate from verified military events prevents the actual Larak strike from being conflated with an unproven assault on Iran's principal oil-export island.

sources.publisher: Lead Stories, authenticity check of the post

events.editor_note: Foregrounded as an example of synthetic media becoming part of the conflict record.
events.research_note: Reuters article opened and read; the separate post-authenticity check was found. The GMA version is a later 31 August update, used retrospectively on the 2 September review date; it must not be represented as all available before an 11:00 BST snapshot. Exact London posting time was not independently resolved. No new Kharg strike is corroborated.

events.title: Bessent outlines planned weekly secondary-sanctions actions
events.summary: In an interview conducted on 30 August and reported on 31 August, Scott Bessent says the U.S. expects new secondary-sanctions actions at roughly weekly intervals, initially focused on banks.
events.context: The weekly cadence was an announced enforcement intention, not proof that a new package had already been imposed every week. Banks were identified as the first focus of an intensified effort to isolate Iranian trade.
details: In a Reuters interview conducted on Sunday, 30 August, Bessent said further secondary-sanctions actions were expected at roughly weekly intervals. The interview was reported on 31 August as the administration broadened the economic campaign announced the previous week.

He discussed penalties involving the UAE branches of Banque Misr and the possibility of wider restrictions on institutions that continued prohibited Iranian business. Proposed future measures must be distinguished from actions already taken. The historical significance is the effort to increase third-country financial pressure while diplomacy remained stalled, not an established guarantee that the campaign would achieve its stated objectives.
events.research_note: Reuters interview report checked. Distinguishes the 30 August interview from its 31 August publication and planned cadence from completed weekly designations. No projection of sanctions effectiveness or legal advice is offered.

revisions.reason: Clarifies the interview/report-date distinction and treats the cadence as a stated plan rather than completed weekly designations.

previous.title: U.S. signals weekly secondary-sanctions actions
previous.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says Washington is moving toward weekly secondary-sanctions actions, initially targeting banks involved in Iranian trade.

events.title: Pezeshkian offers reciprocal return to the June memorandum
events.summary: At the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, Iran's president said Tehran would resume its commitments under the June memorandum if Washington did the same. He did not announce a new agreement.
events.context: The proposal returned the failed June framework to the diplomatic agenda after the Larak Island exchange. Iran continued to link unrestricted passage through Hormuz to U.S. implementation of that agreement.
details: Masoud Pezeshkian made the conditional offer before the broader U.S. strikes later on 1 September. Reuters reported his remarks from Iranian state media. He had also said the previous day that Iran remained open to negotiations.

This was an Iranian negotiating position, not a jointly accepted ceasefire or a confirmed reopening of shipping. The distinction matters when tracing repeated attempts to revive the memorandum after disagreements over its implementation.

relationships.label: Proposal to revive the June framework
relationships.summary: Pezeshkian explicitly referred back to the June memorandum; this link does not imply U.S. acceptance.

events.research_note: The offer is documented by Reuters and AP; implementation was not established. The date is the summit statement, not a new signing.

events.title: U.S. launches a wider round of strikes along Iran's southern coast
events.summary: CENTCOM announced a new operation against IRGC targets, beginning at noon U.S. Eastern time. Washington said it was responding to attempted attacks on shipping and American personnel; Iran subsequently launched regional reprisals.
events.context: The operation followed the 30 August Larak Island strike and broadened the renewed confrontation beyond those two launchers. Washington's explanation focused on threats to ships and U.S. forces around Hormuz.
details: CNN and EFE reported CENTCOM's announcement that strikes began at 12:00 Eastern Daylight Time, equivalent to 16:00 UTC. The command later listed air-defence, radar, maritime, mine-laying and communications targets. These descriptions identify the U.S. military's stated target set, not independently verified damage at every site.

AP reported explosions across southern coastal areas and eyewitness accounts from Bandar Abbas. The wedding casualties and Iranian counterattacks are recorded separately so that the military operation, civilian-harm reports and claimed retaliation remain distinguishable.

media.caption: CENTCOM-supplied missile-launch image accompanying reporting on the September strikes; location and filming time not independently verified.

events.research_note: The timestamp follows CENTCOM's publicly reported start time. The occurrence of strikes is corroborated; military target descriptions and assessments of effectiveness remain attributed to the parties.

events.precision: Evening attack in Iran; casualty reports developed over 1–3 September
events.title: Iran reports wedding guests, including a child, killed in U.S. strike at Kuhestak
events.summary: Iranian officials reported deaths and dozens of injuries at a wedding in Kuhestak, in Sirik County, during the U.S. strikes. By 3 September, Reuters cited the Iranian Red Crescent reporting four killed and 67 wounded.
events.context: Earlier accounts gave five deaths and 68 injuries. These remain attributed casualty reports, not an independently audited final toll. CENTCOM acknowledged the reports and said it did not target civilians; that statement did not resolve how the home was damaged.
details: The Iranian Red Crescent's account carried by Reuters on 3 September put the toll at four killed and 67 wounded. AP reported that Hormozgan deputy governor Ahmad Nafisi described a strike on a home hosting a wedding, with a child among the dead. Reporting placed the incident in Kuhestak, near Sirik on Iran's southern coast, on the evening of 1 September.

Reuters' subsequent reporting used the Red Crescent's figure of four deaths and 67 injuries, while AP's earlier account carried a higher preliminary tally. Reuters said it could not independently verify the incident. The record therefore preserves the different accounts without treating a reported toll, intended target or legal characterization as a settled finding.

claims.claim: Four people killed and 67 wounded at the wedding.
claims.status: Iranian Red Crescent account carried by Reuters on 3 September; not independently verified.

claims.claim: The cited reporting does not establish intentional targeting of wedding guests.
claims.status: Evidence limitation: CENTCOM said it did not target civilians, but no final finding on the incident was available.

Reuters via Internazionale — attribution and verification limits

events.title: Iran retaliates across the region; Jordan and Gulf states report interceptions
events.summary: Iran announced missile and drone attacks on U.S. positions after the 1 September bombardment. Jordan said it intercepted ten of thirteen missiles; Bahrain and Kuwait also reported confronting incoming attacks.
events.context: The regional spread of attacks was established more clearly than Iranian claims about damage or American deaths. A report of incoming weapons is not proof that the claimed base or equipment was destroyed.
details: Jordan's armed-forces statement, published by Petra on 2 September, said thirteen missiles entered its airspace, ten were destroyed and three landed in uninhabited areas, with no casualties reported. Iran described attacks on American positions in Jordan as retaliation for the U.S. strikes.

Reuters also reported Iranian claims concerning Bahrain, Kuwait and Iraq. U.S. officials said preliminary assessments showed no American casualties, contradicting Iranian claims of deaths in Jordan and northern Iraq. AP reported Kuwaiti interceptions and Bahrain's statement that it had intercepted the attacks directed at it.

claims.claim: Iran killed American personnel in the counterattacks.
claims.status: Not independently corroborated; U.S. officials reported no casualties in their initial assessments.

relationships.label: Iran's stated response to the U.S. strikes
relationships.summary: Iran explicitly presented its counterattacks as retaliation. The connection does not verify its claimed battlefield results.

events.research_note: Covers the overnight 1–2 September sequence. Jordan's interception count is its official account. Claims of destroyed aircraft or American deaths are not converted into confirmed losses.

events.title: U.S. officials describe attacks on two Iranian tankers under a retaliatory policy
events.summary: U.S. officials told Axios that two Iranian government tankers were attacked in the 1 September operation under a new policy of responding to tanker attacks with tanker strikes.
events.context: The reported rationale differed from disabling ships for attempting to breach the blockade. It connected maritime attacks to an explicit reciprocal targeting policy, whose adoption was attributed to officials rather than a published order.
details: The War Zone examined CENTCOM footage that appeared to show two vessels being struck. It reported that a command spokesperson referred questions about a new policy to policymakers; CENTCOM's public target list did not specifically name oil tankers.

The evidence supports recording the officials' account and the military-supplied imagery. It does not independently establish the vessels' identities, cargoes, final condition or whether the reported policy deterred subsequent attacks.

sources.publisher: The War Zone — footage review and CENTCOM response

events.research_note: Dated to the reported 1 September operation, not the 2 September article. The War Zone cites Axios for the policy; it is not a second independent confirmation of that decision.

events.precision: Approximate incident time; deaths announced on 2 September
events.title: Attack on Saudi tanker Sidr kills two Filipino seafarers; deaths disclosed on 2 September
events.summary: Bahri announced on 2 September that two Filipino crew members had died in an incident involving its tanker Sidr while transiting Hormuz late on 31 August. Saudi Arabia blamed Iran.
events.context: The fatalities were disclosed after the previous data cutoff but belong on the date of the incident. The company's confirmation of deaths and the Saudi government's attribution are separate pieces of evidence.
details: Bahri placed the incident at approximately 23:40 local time on 31 August, reported by the BBC as 19:40 UTC. Reuters and AFP carried the company's subsequent announcement that two seafarers had died. Bahri's initial statement did not describe the weapon or all circumstances of the attack.

The BBC reported maritime-security accounts of projectile impacts on Sidr and another tanker, Senegal Prosperity. Saudi Arabia publicly attributed the Sidr attack to Iran. This is not treated as proof of a separate Iranian claim that two ships struck mines on 2 September.
events.research_note: Late-reported 31 August event, appended without moving older records. The time is approximate. The crew deaths were acknowledged by the operator; the record attributes responsibility to Saudi Arabia rather than declaring an independently established finding.

events.title: Trump predicts a short renewed campaign but sets no deadline to end strikes
events.summary: Trump said the renewed military effort against Iran would not last much longer, without setting an end date. He emphasized shipping through Hormuz and said election considerations did not determine his decisions.
events.context: This was a presidential forecast, not an announced ceasefire or a binding timetable. The absence of a date distinguishes it from earlier deadline events in the ledger.
details: ABC News reported the remarks on the afternoon of 2 September. Asked how much longer the campaign would continue, Trump offered no specific duration. When questioned about remaining targets, he pointed to U.S. efforts to move ships and oil through Hormuz.
The statement should not be used to infer an operational halt. Any subsequent cessation of attacks, negotiation or ceasefire requires its own evidence and event record.

sources.publisher: ABC News — 2 September, 3:46 p.m. EDT update

events.research_note: Records the public statement, not a verified prediction. No exact end date was given in the cited account.

events.title: UN chief calls for a halt to fighting after reports of wedding casualties
events.summary: António Guterres, through spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric, expressed alarm at renewed U.S.–Iran fighting and reported civilian casualties, including the wedding incident. He urged an immediate end to military action and renewed diplomacy.
events.context: The UN response placed civilian protection alongside the regional escalation. Concern about reported casualties is not the same as an independent investigation establishing a toll or a court finding on responsibility.
details: At the 2 September briefing, Dujarric said the secretary-general condemned attacks on civilians and called on the parties to meet their obligations to protect them. Anadolu and Europa Press both reported the statement.

The appeal warned against further escalation and called for restraint and negotiations. This entry records that diplomatic intervention, without converting the spokesperson's reference to a reported wedding strike into separate forensic confirmation of the incident.

relationships.label: Civilian-harm reports prompt UN concern
relationships.summary: The spokesperson explicitly referred to the reported wedding strike while urging a halt to fighting.

events.research_note: The public briefing was cross-checked in two news-agency accounts. It was an appeal, not a ceasefire agreement or judicial ruling.

events.title: Kuwait reports fresh Iranian attacks; Tehran also claims a strike on a UAE base
events.summary: Kuwait said its air defences were confronting Iranian missiles and drones early on 3 September. Iran claimed attacks on Ahmed al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and Al Minhad Air Base in the UAE.
events.context: This was a further reported attack sequence after the 1–2 September reprisals. Kuwait's acknowledgment of incoming fire does not independently verify Iran's account of particular targets or damage in either country.
details: ABC News reported Iran's statement naming communications equipment, stores and aircraft hangars in Kuwait, as well as troop positions and radar in the UAE. Kuwait separately acknowledged incoming weapons and air-defence activity.

AFP described the renewed attacks as occurring despite U.S. warnings of further strikes. The cited reporting did not establish the damage claimed at individual bases or an independently verified casualty total for this new wave.

sources.publisher: ABC News — Iranian claims and Kuwait's statement

relationships.label: Further attacks in the same escalation sequence
relationships.summary: The fresh 3 September reports follow the previous regional counterattacks; each wave retains its own evidence and date.

events.research_note: Checked against reporting available on 3 September. The UAE-target claim is not treated as independently confirmed, and this is not a relabelling of the earlier 31 August Al Minhad claim.

events.title: Reuters reports mounting Iranian financial strain from the blockade and sanctions
events.summary: Three senior Iranian sources told Reuters that restrictions on oil exports and overseas financing were becoming harder to withstand. The report described pressure on trade, currency access and fuel supplies, not a new sanctions announcement.
events.context: The date marks publication of a significant economic assessment. It does not imply that the underlying strain began on 3 September or that an eventual diplomatic concession was inevitable.
details: A 1 September Reuters review, drawing on Kpler, Vortexa and TankerTrackers.com, had reported about seven weeks without meaningful Iranian crude exports through Hormuz. That finding concerned shipments passing the blockade, not every barrel loaded, held offshore or moved through other routes.

The 3 September report described constrained access to foreign currency and intermediaries charging more to handle Iranian trade. One senior source estimated roughly two months of gasoline supply remained. That reserve estimate was an attributed, unverified claim, not an independently measured countdown to fuel exhaustion.

sources.publisher: Reuters via AOL — 1 September tanker-tracking review

events.research_note: A dated reporting milestone using two different Reuters reports, not two independent news organizations. The anonymous officials' assessments and fuel-reserve estimate remain attributed. No prediction that sanctions will force an agreement is adopted.
